title: Tracing an ASP.NET Core service
summary: AddOpenTelemetry().WithTracing(): the SDK, the ASP.NET Core instrumentation, your own ActivitySource, and the reasons spans silently go missing.

steps.title: One call wires the SDK
body: In an ASP.NET Core app the SDK is a service registration (package `OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting`, version 1.20 here):
```csharp
builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
.ConfigureResource(r => r.AddService("orders", serviceVersion: "2.1.0"))
.WithTracing(t => t
.AddSource("Orders.Api")                 // your own ActivitySource(s); wildcards work: "Orders.*"
.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()          // a Server span per request (OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore)
.AddHttpClientInstrumentation()          // a Client span per outgoing call
.AddOtlpExporter());                     // to the Collector; reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* from the environment
- The **instrumentation** packages subscribe to what ASP.NET Core and HttpClient already emit and turn it into spans with the stable
HTTP conventions (`http.route`, `http.response.status_code`, `url.path`, `error.type`).
- `AddSource` is an allow-list: the SDK listens **only** to sources you name. Database libraries ship their own (`AddNpgsql()`,
`AddSource("Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore")` with `OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.EntityFrameworkCore`, still a beta package).
- `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` and the exporter variables override or complement the code,
so operations can change them without a rebuild (the live lab does exactly that).
In these exercises you need **no exporter**: the tests add their own processor to the tracer provider you build and read what it
exports. Everything you see under the results came out of the real SDK.

hints: `builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()` returns a builder: chain `.ConfigureResource(...)` and `.WithTracing(...)` on it.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var server = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Server);
Dojo.Check("a server span was exported", server is not null, "No span reached the tracer provider. Did you call AddOpenTelemetry().WithTracing(t => t.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation())?");
Dojo.Eq("its name is method + route template", "GET /orders/{id:int}", server?.DisplayName);
Dojo.Eq("the resource says service.name = orders", "orders", DojoOtel.Service(server));

steps.prompt: A teammate added `var activity = Source.StartActivity("price order");` and `AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()`, but no `price order` span ever appears. The server spans do. Most likely cause?
options: The tracer provider has no `AddSource("Orders.Api")`, so nobody listens to that ActivitySource and StartActivity returns null
Custom spans need their own exporter
The span name contains a space
steps.explain: The SDK only listens to sources it was told about. Forgetting `AddSource` (or a typo in the name) is the most common "my spans are missing" bug; it fails silently because `?.` swallows the null. A test that asserts the span exists, like the ones here, catches it.

steps.title: Your own spans: one ActivitySource per component
body: Create one `ActivitySource` per library or component, as a static, named like a namespace, and register the same name with `AddSource`:
```csharp
static class Telemetry
public static readonly ActivitySource Source = new("Orders.Api");
app.MapPost("/orders/{id:int}/price", (int id, string? coupon) =>
using var activity = Telemetry.Source.StartActivity("price order");   // child of the request's server span
activity?.SetTag("app.order.id", id);
if (coupon == "EXPIRED")
activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Error, "coupon expired");
activity?.SetTag("error.type", "coupon_expired");
return Results.BadRequest();
return Results.Ok(new { id, total = 37.5 });
- `StartActivity` makes the new span a child of `Activity.Current` (the server span), and `using` ends it.
- Add attributes that answer the questions you will be asked in an incident (which order, which plan, how many items), typed as what
they are. Prefix your own with your namespace (`app.`).
- For an exception: `activity?.AddException(ex)` (.NET 9+) records it as an `exception` event with type, message and stack trace.
- The 400 above is a *client* error for the server span (status stays Unset); your own span can still say what went wrong.

steps.prompt: Good span attribute, or does it belong somewhere else?
items: the whole request body as JSON (40 KB)
steps.explain: Ids and small facts that explain behaviour are what spans are for: each span is one request, so high cardinality is fine there (unlike metrics). Secrets and payment data never go into telemetry; big payloads cost money and leak data. Most backends truncate long values anyway.

steps.title: A span for the pricing step
prompt: Add `POST /orders/{id:int}/price?coupon=...` to the service (keep the tracing setup from the previous step):
- create a static `ActivitySource` named **`Orders.Api`** and register it with the tracer provider;
- in the endpoint, a span **`price order`** with the attribute **`app.order.id`** (an **int**);
- when `coupon` is `EXPIRED`: span status **Error** with the description **`coupon expired`**, attribute **`error.type`** =
solution: public static readonly ActivitySource Source = new("Orders.Api");
hints: Two places must agree on the name: `new ActivitySource("Orders.Api")` and `.AddSource("Orders.Api")` (or `.AddSource(Telemetry.Source.Name)`).
`activity?.SetTag("app.order.id", id);` keeps the int. For the error: `SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Error, "coupon expired")` and `SetTag("error.type", "coupon_expired")`.
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var price = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "price order");

Dojo.Check("a price order span was exported", price is not null, "Spans exported: " + string.Join(", ", DojoOtel.Spans.Select(a => a.DisplayName)) + ". Is the ActivitySource registered with AddSource?");
Dojo.Eq("it comes from the Orders.Api source", "Orders.Api", price.Source.Name);
Dojo.Check("app.order.id is the int 7", price.GetTagItem("app.order.id") is int dojoId && dojoId == 7, "got " + price.GetTagItem("app.order.id")?.GetType().Name);
var server = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Server && a.TraceId == price.TraceId);
Dojo.Check("it is a child of the request's server span", server is not null && price.ParentSpanId == server.SpanId, "");
Dojo.Eq("a good coupon leaves the status Unset", "Unset", price.Status.ToString());
var failed = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.DisplayName == "price order" && Equals(a.GetTagItem("app.order.id"), 8));
var badServer = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Server && failed != null && a.TraceId == failed.TraceId);
Dojo.Eq("the server span of a 400 stays Unset (a client error)", "Unset", badServer?.Status.ToString());
